mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of PAYEMS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a single month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals a weakening demand coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS > 2%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST decline and high FEDFUNDS on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between sustained CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) decline by more than 1% in a single month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, it signals a weakening demand coupled with a poor labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 1% in 1 month AND UNRATE > 7%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of RSAFS decline and high UNRATE on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
